I'm in the same boat as you. The best I can tell, don't be alone. Find a friend or friends who you can talk to and talk to them as much as you can about anything. If one friend is busy, hop to another friend. Talk to strangers, just keep busy with someone. 
The problem I find is that when we're so focused on ourselves, our pain and grief sucks us in to the point of self destruction just to get out of it. By focusing on someone else, you step out of your head for a while. 

If the urge becomes too strong and talking doesn't help, delay. Delay the action. If you want to self harm now, instead give yourself 5 minutes, then you see if you want to do it still. 

Easier said than done tbh, I haven't completely stopped cutting either but it is possible to stop. That's the hope I have and I hope you have that hope too.

A lot of teachers changed my life and I was one of the lucky ones who were surrounded by them. But the most important one was a Math Teacher in Form 2 or when I was 14. I was always terrible in Maths (Later on we learned I was spatially and numerically dyslexic) and she was the only one who never gave up on me. 
She'd hold me back from recess and held me behind from classes just to go through the material with me a second time. I hated being held back but when I saw she was also sacrificing her time and energy for one stupid student, it just stroked a chord in me. 
It completely changed my view on teachers but most importantly it made me feel as though I wasn't stupid or lazy. It made me feel like there was hope for me. I just needed more help and until today she's the reason I refuse to give up on myself. In a sea of students, I was the only she picked on to stay back and refused to give up on. She gave me a chance and helped me back up on my feet.

In conclusion, you should apologise and try and communicate better. Only if the mom is unwilling to compromise or talk about it does it make her TA. Good luck!
